neighbours.label: ' open' as a modifier before a noun naming an open-access offer or event (open bar, open house, open mic, open swim, open play); not the verb 'open' and not predicate 'open' (stays open, left open)
fire: Tickets to the gala cost sixty dollars and include an open bar.
The fire station is holding an open house for families next weekend.
On Thursdays the cafe hosts an open mic for local poets.
The climbing gym has open climb sessions every evening after six.
The reception featured a buffet dinner and a two-hour open bar.
Parents can tour the classrooms during the open house in October.
The rink offers open skate on Sunday afternoons for five dollars.
She first sang in public at an open mic in a college basement.
quiet: Tickets to the gala cost sixty dollars and include a drink at the bar.
The fire station will open its doors to families next weekend.
On Thursdays the cafe stays open late for local poets.
The climbing gym is open every evening after six.
The reception featured a buffet dinner and a two-hour dance set.
Parents can open the classroom windows during the hot days in October.
The rink was left open on Sunday afternoon by mistake.
She first sang in public at a talent show in a college basement.
